science|whole|0: By employing physical and weak regularity conditions, this work classifies and unifies all possible spherically symmetric dust spacetimes in general relativity. It provides junction conditions for general non-comoving, non-null surfaces and establishes the limits of kinematical quantities on all comoving surfaces with Darmois matching. The study demonstrates that an inhomogeneous generalization of the Kantowski-Sachs metric can be joined to the Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi metric. Furthermore, all possible spacetimes are categorized into four topological groups, including those with 3-torus spatial sections, and the recollapse conjecture for these spacetimes emerges naturally from this framework.
science|whole|1: Starting from a basic description of vortices and pinning centers without electrodynamical assumptions, we derive nonlinear vortex density profiles in type-II dirty superconductors under varying external magnetic fields. These results validate a modified Bean model, specifically adhering to the Kim empirical form relating internal current to the local magnetic field. Furthermore, we produce realistic magnetization hysteresis loops and analyze the discrete evolution of density profiles. This evolution is non-continuous, occurring instead through vortex avalanches triggered by the addition or removal of vortices at the system's edges.
science|whole|2: A structural model is proposed for intermediate-sized silicon clusters that generates unique, dangling-bond-free structures. This model features a five-atom bulk-like core surrounded by a fullerene-like surface, where the reconstruction of ideal fullerene geometry produces crown atoms surrounded by $\pi$-bonded dimer pairs. This framework accounts for the unique, stable structures of $\text{Si}_{33}$, $\text{Si}_{39}$, and $\text{Si}_{45}$ clusters, explaining their low reactivity toward the chemisorption of ammonia, methanol, ethylene, and water. Furthermore, the model aligns with experimental evidence showing a transition from prolate to spherical shapes at $\text{Si}_{27}$ and explains reagent-specific chemisorption reactivities based on the electronic structures of the reagents.
science|whole|3: We present results for two types of high-order neural connections that serve as corrections to the Hopfield model. Using replica mean-field theory, we analyze the equilibrium properties and compare them with numerical simulations. We provide an optimal learning algorithm for fourth-order connections that enhances storage capacity without increasing the weight of the higher-order term. While one model qualitatively resembles the original Hopfield model, the other exhibits a rich new behavior: depending on the temperature and the strength of the fourth-order connections, the system displays several phase transitions and two distinct retrieval regions separated by a gap. Furthermore, the spin glass states appear to vanish above a specific load parameter value, $\alpha_g$.
science|whole|4: Inspired by the evolution of complex bird songs, this study proposes an abstract imitation game to investigate the emergence of dynamical complexity. In this model, artificial "birds" display "song" time series to one another, with winners determined by their ability to accurately imitate their peers. By incorporating population dynamics based on game scores and parameter mutations within the song dynamics, the system evolves toward the boundary between chaos and periodic windows, characterized by punctuated equilibria. The results highlight the significance of the "edge of chaos" and topological chaos in fostering complexity.
science|whole|5: The precise formulation of tree-adjoining grammar (TAG) derivations significantly impacts various applications, including syntactic analysis, semantic interpretation, and statistical language modeling. We contend that the current definition of TAG derivations requires reformulation to accurately reflect linguistic dependencies. We propose a definition of TAG derivations as equivalence classes of ordered derivation trees, which is both mathematically precise and computationally practical, as it allows for compilation into linear indexed grammars with efficient recognition and parsing algorithms.
science|whole|6: This paper explores the fundamental problems of algorithmic algebraic number theory, focusing on mathematical theory rather than practical implementation. We review existing progress and identify remaining challenges in the field. Our goal is to demonstrate that algorithmic study enhances both our understanding of and interest in algebraic number fields. The discussion centers on three primary topics: determining Galois groups, identifying the ring of integers of an algebraic number field, and computing the group of units and the class group of that ring of integers.
science|whole|7: Assume a target function is monotonic (weakly increasing) and an initial estimate of this function is available that is not weakly increasing, a common occurrence in many statistical estimation methods. We demonstrate that these estimates can be improved without loss of accuracy using rearrangement techniques. Both univariate and multivariate rearrangement methods transform the original estimate into a monotonic one, resulting in an estimate that is closer to the true curve across common metrics. We illustrate these findings through both a computational example and an empirical analysis of age-height growth charts.
science|whole|8: Recent progress in diverse interdisciplinary fields, including astrophysics, cosmogeophysics, and nuclear geology, has fueled significant developments in the non-organic theory of petroleum genesis. This theory proposes that petroleum originates from abiogenic primordial sources, offering explanations for specific geological features that the standard organic framework struggles to account for. If this non-organic theory is validated, it would imply that hydrocarbon reserves are vast and nearly inexhaustible.
science|whole|9: Random stepped frequency (RSF) radar, characterized by the transmission of pulses with random frequencies, is capable of suppressing range ambiguity, enhancing covert detection, and providing robust electronic counter-countermeasures (ECCM) [1]. This paper employs a sparse recovery method to estimate the range and Doppler of targets and introduces a cognitive mechanism to further optimize the performance of this sparse recovery approach. Under this mechanism, the carrier frequencies of the transmitted pulses are adaptively designed based on the observed environment. We investigate the criteria for designing these carrier frequencies and develop efficient methodologies for their implementation. Simulation results indicate that the adaptive frequency-design mechanism significantly improves target reconstruction performance compared to non-adaptive methods.
